text:
sam: Quick sync 1: we have recurring support tickets about 'preview' vs 'apply' semantics for runtime configs. Can we lock a contract and what telemetry to emit?

marta: Important. Console preview currently returns a diff + simulated routing but doesn't leave a clear trail. Support wants an auditable id.

dyson: I purposely avoided making preview emit the same metrics as a real rollout (would pollute SLOs). But we should definitely record an audit event and small-sample telemetry.

sam: Proposal: preview = read-only dry-run. Emits: 1) audit log (actor, config_id, preview_id, payload hash), 2) preview_telemetry counter (sampled at 1%), 3) no effects on quota accounting or routing metrics.

ops-bot: FYI: deploy-bot blocks preview attempts that change protected keys (routing.weights, billing.tier).

laura: API shape idea: POST /v1/configs/preview -> { preview_id, diff, route_simulation, warnings }. Example:

```
curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/configs/preview' \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
 -d '{"target":"staging","config":{...}}'
```

laura: preview_id must surface in console and logs so we can trace back.

ankur: Sampling: 1% for general previews is fine. For previews touching sensitive fields (auth, quotas, kms) we need forced 100% logging. Suggest marking keys as sensitive in schema and have preview endpoint escalate sampling.

marta: Agreed. We'll keep a sensitive-key registry and the server will bump sampling for those previews.

ryan: Console UX: show a "PREVIEW (not applied)" pill with preview_id, link to expand diff, and a button "Promote to canary" that preserves the preview's cohort and sampling.

sam: About atomicity: teams expect apply to be transactional. Reality: apply is eventually consistent across regions. We should document that apply is best-effort atomic within a region; cross-region fanout may lag.

dyson: We already validate schema/routing constraints server-side. Propose adding a synchronous preflight mode: run simulation with a short timeout (5s), fail apply if simulation finds constraint violations. This reduces surprises.

laura: Implementation detail: accept header X-Config-Mode: preview|preflight|apply. Preflight executes simulator and returns 409 + details on constraint failures. Timeout 5s.

ankur: Dashboards: add a "Pending changes" timeline in Config History showing previews, preflights (pass/fail), and applies. Telemetry should carry preview_id/preflight_id tags so we can correlate.

marta: Rollout flow: when promoting preview->canary preserve the exact delta and store an immutable snapshot. Also produce an estimated impact (cost/qps) during preview so owners can decide.

ryan: Edge case: preview suggests routing move that overloads a tiny pool. We need a pre-apply capacity check: if expected qps on pool > cap*headroom, fail preflight with guidance (increase pool, enable fallback).

dyson: We have capacity metrics and a conservative headroom. We'll implement a lightweight capacity guard in preflight and return clear remediation steps.

sam: Action items: 1) Laura: draft API response and header semantics + preview_id; 2) Dyson/Ankur: backend audit event, sampled preview telemetry, forced logging for sensitive keys, preflight simulation + capacity guard; 3) Ryan/Marta: console badge, promote-to-canary flow that preserves cohorts + pending changes timeline; 4) Marta: RFC doc with wire format and telemetry event names.

marta: I'll open the RFC and assign owners. Will include example telemetry events: config.preview.request, config.preview.sampled, config.preflight.result, config.apply.attempt.

sam: Cool. Tagging @dyson @laura @ankur @ryan. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: next config deploy window Tue 02:00 UTC. Preflights must finish before window to be included.
